title: Zephyrine and the Inheritance
premise: When a confession letter arrives at the taxi depot postmarked the day after old matriarch Zephyrine Ashcombe's funeral, night dispatcher Casper Whitlock realizes the 'accidental' death was anything but—and that the letter names a witness the whole town insists died years ago. As Casper follows the taxi logs he's kept for a decade, he discovers the witness is alive, hidden in plain sight, and that the Ashcombe inheritance has already begun corrupting those who stand to gain it, including the woman Casper has quietly loved for years. In the climax, Casper corners the killer at the abandoned Ashcombe estate during the reading of the will, where the witness—Zephyrine's supposedly dead sister—steps out of the shadows to testify. The killer is the town's beloved doctor, and the inheritance is redirected to fund the shelter Zephyrine always intended, leaving Casper to choose love over the safe, invisible life he built.
about_author: Marguerite Winterbourne is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper archivist who spent fifteen years cataloguing obituaries, wills, and the quiet scandals between them. She writes mysteries about the secrets ordinary people file away and the extraordinary moments they surface.

chapters.title: Postmarked the Day After
chapters.summary: Casper Whitlock's POV. Sorting the depot's mail on his night shift, Casper finds a confession letter addressed to Zephyrine Ashcombe—arriving the day after her funeral, claiming her death was murder and naming a witness everyone believes dead. When the letter's sender is found drowned within hours, Casper realizes he's holding evidence someone will kill to retrieve. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant obligation as the file-keeper of secrets becomes keeper of a lethal one.

chapters.title: The Route Nobody Rides
chapters.summary: Alternating Casper's POV with excerpts from his old taxi logs. Casper traces a decade of fares to a route that ends at the derelict Ashcombe estate, discovering regular pickups of a woman who officially died seven years ago. Meanwhile, heirs circle the will, and his old flame Vera Ashcombe—Zephyrine's niece—warns him to stop digging. Emotional beat: obsession tightening into purpose, and love complicated by suspicion as Vera seems to know more than she admits.

chapters.title: What the Doctor Ordered
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, with a tense mid-chapter shift to the witness hiding in the estate's carriage house. Casper confirms Dr. Edmund Hale—Zephyrine's trusted physician and executor—falsified the death certificate and has been quietly bleeding the estate for years; now he's hunting the witness before Friday's will reading. When Casper's depot is ransacked and his logs stolen, the hunt turns on him. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance as Casper commits fully, choosing the truth over his safe anonymity.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Will
chapters.summary: Climax and resolution, Casper's POV. At the will reading in the Ashcombe mansion, Casper springs his trap: the 'dead' witness, Zephyrine's sister Odile, emerges to testify, and Hale, cornered, confesses the murder before attempting to flee through the estate's flooded cellars. The will's true provision redirects the fortune to the women's shelter Zephyrine always planned, with Vera at its helm. Casper, no longer invisible, asks Vera to stay—and for the first time, chooses love over duty to the files. Emotional beat: catharsis, justice, and earned tenderness.
